chunks: Ahmad ibn Hawtha, Abu Sulayman, narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

The companions of al-Qa'im will be three hundred and thirteen men, sons of the Persians (foreigners). Some of them will be carried on the clouds during the day, known by their name, their father's name, their lineage, and their appearance. Some of them will be asleep on their beds, and they will arrive in Mecca without any prior appointment.

key_terms.أَوْلَادُ الْعَجَمِ: Sons of the Persians/Foreigners, indicating their ethnic origin
key_terms.السَّحَابِ: The clouds, referring to the miraculous mode of transport
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the location of their gathering

ai.seo_question: Who are the 313 companions of al-Qa'im and what are their characteristics?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir specifies that the core army of al-Qa'im will consist of 313 Persian men, a number echoing the companions of Prophet Muhammad at Badr, thereby establishing a lineage of divine victory. It emphasizes their miraculous nature, describing how some are transported by clouds during the day while others appear suddenly in Mecca from sleep, illustrating the concept of *ghaybah* (occultation) and divine preparation. This highlights the Shia belief in the supernatural support granted to the Imam during his final campaign to establish justice.
